answer: Picture an atlas of every registered agent. At random moments the network lights an ember: every identity on the map must solve a fresh, compute-heavy task inside the same ninety-second window. One honest agent pays for one solve; an attacker hiding fifty puppets must rent fifty times the peak compute at that exact instant or watch most of them miss the deadline and lose standing. No identity gets a haven from the next surprise round, so faking a crowd costs as much as being one.
